solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Battled healthy criminal? You’ll be lucky! (6,2,3,3)

indicatorNotes.criminal: a criminal version of the letters is a corrupted one

annotation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea of a fit, fighting crook ever turning up.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark hides a break: everything before it is wordplay, and the exclamation after it is the whole definition, a scornful retort.
annotation.definitionFit: Both phrases are sceptical retorts meaning the hoped-for thing will never happen.

entries.clue: Opening up every lunchtime in store shows real devotion (4,4)

indicatorNotes.Opening: the opening of each word is its first letter
indicatorNotes.in: the letters go inside the store

blocks.note: a trove is a store of treasure
first letters of up, every, lunchtime

annotation.surface: A shop that opens even over the lunch hour shows real commitment to its customers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Store' looks like a shop that stays open; it is a TROVE, and the opening letters go inside it.
annotation.definitionFit: A word-for-word match: true pairs with real, and love with devotion.

entries.clue: What dinner host may ask nowadays (7)

blocks.note: a host's two-word question offering second helpings
an adverb for 'at present', used after a negative

annotation.surface: A remark on what hosts ask their dinner guests these days.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nowadays' looks like part of the dinner-party sentence; it is a separate definition. Split in two, the answer is the host's 'Any more?'
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the spoken offer 'any more?', and the adverb as in 'nobody writes letters anymore', meaning these days.

entries.clue: Spindles I only partly wound (6)

indicatorNotes.only partly: only part of the words is used

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of spindles, through I, into the start of only

annotation.surface: Someone admits to winding their spindles only halfway.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wound' reads as the past tense of wind, fitting spindles; here it is the noun, an injury.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain medical synonym: a lesion is any damaged area of tissue, such as a wound.

entries.clue: Request to take part in live attempts at wickerworks (10)

indicatorNotes.to take part in: to take part in something is to go inside it

annotation.surface: Someone asks to join live attempts at weaving baskets.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Live' reads as an adjective, as in a live event; it is the verb 'to be', which splits open for the request.
annotation.definitionFit: Basketry is the craft or product of weaving wicker, so basketries are wickerworks.

entries.clue: You leave a content creator to listen to instrument (4)

indicatorNotes.leave: when you leave a place you are no longer in it, so the letters of YOU go
indicatorNotes.to listen to: what is heard, not what is written

blocks.note: the two sound the same in a British accent that drops the final R

annotation.surface: An instruction to walk out on an online content creator and go listen to some music.
annotation.walkthrough: A content creator here is a YouTuber, someone who posts videos. The sound match relies on non-rhotic British speech, where 'tuber' and 'tuba' are said alike.
annotation.definitionFit: A general term for a specific item: the tuba is one brass instrument among many.

entries.clue: Scottish island contains real common (8)

indicatorNotes.contains: the island holds the other word inside it

blocks.note: Eday is one of the Orkney islands
very = real, actual, as in 'the very man'

annotation.surface: A Scottish island has plenty of real common land.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Common' looks like a stretch of shared land on the island; it is the adjective, meaning ordinary.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the adjective sense: something common or everyday is ordinary and routine.

entries.clue: Falcons’ home lacking a hunter (7)

indicatorNotes.lacking: the hunter is without one A

blocks.note: ATALANTA, the huntress of Greek myth, minus one A

annotation.surface: A falcon's nest stands empty because it lacks a hunting bird.
annotation.walkthrough: The Falcons are an American football team, not birds. Atalanta was the swift huntress of Greek legend; 'a' is the A she loses.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by association: the city is home ground to an NFL team named the Falcons.

entries.clue: Start to develop extremely dishy friend (5)

indicatorNotes.extremely: take the extremes, the first and last letters

blocks.note: to bud is to begin to grow

annotation.surface: Someone begins to fall for a very attractive friend.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dishy' is British slang for good-looking. 'Start to develop' is one verb phrase, BUD, not a first-letter instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal, chiefly American synonym: a buddy is a close friend or pal.

entries.clue: Grant could be for classic work (7)

blocks.note: the first name of the US Civil War general and president Grant

annotation.surface: A grant might be awarded for a piece of classic writing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grant' reads as funding; it is Ulysses S. Grant, and 'could be' says his first name can stand for him.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the forename of General Grant, and Joyce's modernist novel, itself named after Homer's hero.

entries.clue: Silesian city — macabre slaughterhouses (7)

blocks.note: the letters run from the tail of macabre into the head of slaughterhouses

annotation.surface: A city in Silesia is known for its grim abattoirs.
annotation.walkthrough: There is no indicator word; the dash sets the city beside the phrase it hides in. Breslau is the German name of Wrocław, now in Poland.
annotation.definitionFit: A historic name: Breslau was the German name for Wrocław, the chief city of Silesia.

entries.clue: Check sweetheart’s embracing acceptable second cousin (4,4)

indicatorNotes.embracing: the sweetheart's arms go round the other letters

annotation.surface: A check on whether a lover is hugging a second cousin, which would be allowed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Second cousin' looks like a relative; it is the second letter of 'cousin'. The 's after sweetheart is 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: A phrasal-verb synonym: to check a document is to examine it quickly.

entries.clue: Celebrated that my end has started badly (6)

indicatorNotes.started: the start of 'has' is its first letter
indicatorNotes.badly: the letters are put together badly

annotation.surface: Someone rejoices that their life's final chapter has begun poorly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Has started' reads as part of the sentence, but it only supplies the first letter of 'has'; 'that' joins the definition to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: To hymn is to praise in song, so the past tense matches celebrated in the sense of extolled.

entries.clue: Spending too much is obvious holding move (4,6)

indicatorNotes.holding: the outer word holds the other inside

annotation.surface: A claim that overspending is plain to see when you won't budge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Holding move' sounds like a tactic in chess or wrestling; 'holding' is the instruction, and 'move' is the word held.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive phrase: a project over budget has spent more than it was allowed.

entries.clue: Turning every unending turn (4)

indicatorNotes.unending: without its end: drop the last letter
indicatorNotes.Turning: the letters are turned into a new order

annotation.surface: A picture of endless turning, every way at once.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turning' at the start looks like the definition; it rearranges the letters, and the definition is the last word.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for a change of direction, usually a sudden one.

entries.clue: Started hole with a method that’s outlawed (5,4)

blocks.note: in golf you start each hole by driving off the tee

annotation.surface: Someone began digging a hole using a technique that has been banned.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hole' suggests digging; it is a golf hole, begun with a drive. The definition is the past tense, as with banishing someone.
annotation.definitionFit: A historical sense: to outlaw someone was to banish them, driving them out of society.

entries.clue: Rich source of excitement (4-2-2)

blocks.note: a well is a source (of water)
a to-do is a fuss, a commotion

annotation.surface: Something described as a plentiful supply of thrills.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rich' looks like it describes the source, as in 'a rich source'; it is the definition on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for prosperous: the well-to-do are comfortably off.

entries.clue: Hair in tonsorial centre is an aggravation (8)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places the hair inside the letters from tonsorial
indicatorNotes.centre: the centre of the word is its middle letters

blocks.note: a tress is a lock of hair

annotation.surface: Finding hair everywhere in the barber's shop is a nuisance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tonsorial' means to do with barbers, so the surface puts hair in a barber's shop; here only its middle three letters are used.
annotation.definitionFit: A psychological term: a stressor is anything that causes stress, such as an aggravation.

entries.clue: Trump — maybe cheer? (4,5)

blocks.note: in a card game, when hearts are trumps you may win a trick with one
a verb: to be encouraged, cheer up

annotation.surface: A question whether Trump might raise a cheer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trump' looks like the politician; it is the card-game verb, and 'maybe' marks hearts as just one possible trump suit.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: literally taking a trick with a heart, and the idiom for regaining courage.

entries.clue: Offensive fool gets no tip for poor service (7)

indicatorNotes.gets no tip: the word loses its tip, its first letter

blocks.note: a FAULT is a bad serve in tennis; without its tip it is AULT

annotation.surface: A rude idiot of a customer gives no tip after bad service.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tip' and 'service' suggest a restaurant; the service is a tennis serve, and the tip is a first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A military sense: 'offensive' is the noun for an attack, and an assault is one.

entries.clue: Top batter exhausted (4)

blocks.note: to top a rival's score is to better it
to batter is to strike repeatedly, a third meaning

annotation.surface: The best batsman in a cricket team is worn out.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is cricket, where the top batter opens the innings; in fact each word is its own meaning of the answer, making three definitions.
annotation.definitionFit: Three senses of one word: to surpass, to strike repeatedly, and (informally) tired out.

entries.clue: Talk at length about being left out of drunken sex with pilot (7)

indicatorNotes.being left out of: L, for left, is taken out
indicatorNotes.drunken: the letters stagger into a new order

annotation.surface: A scandal story: someone goes on and on about a drunken fling with a pilot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left' does double duty as the abbreviation L and the sense 'left out'; 'with' just joins the two fodder words.
annotation.definitionFit: A formal verb: to exposit is to expound, setting out a subject in detail.

entries.clue: Hand in religious Christmas decoration (5)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' puts the hand inside the religious word

blocks.note: L = left, as in left hand

annotation.surface: Religious Christmas decorations being handed round.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hand' usually gives H; here it is L, the left hand, as in the L and R of hand markings.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the spiky-leaved evergreen is one traditional Christmas decoration.

entries.clue: Section of orchestra taking A level (6)

annotation.definitionNote: strata is plural; the singular is stratum, a level

indicatorNotes.Section of: a section is a piece of the words

blocks.note: the letters run from the tail of orchestra into the head of taking

annotation.surface: A part of the orchestra is sitting an A-level exam.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Section of orchestra' looks like the strings or brass; it is a slice of the words. 'A level' reads as a British school exam taken at 18.
annotation.definitionFit: A geological sense: strata are layers of rock, each one a level.

entries.clue: Tragically lose US fliers (6)

indicatorNotes.Tragically: the letters come to a tragic, broken end

annotation.surface: An American airline sadly loses its pilots.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fliers' suggests aviators; it means birds.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: ousels, such as the ring ousel and the blackbird, are birds, and birds fly.

entries.clue: Petrol’s final extra input into hybrid’s manifold (8)

indicatorNotes.final: the final letter of petrol is the one used
indicatorNotes.input into: something input into a machine goes inside it

blocks.note: a mule is a hybrid of horse and donkey
a tip is an extra payment

annotation.surface: A car mechanic's note: petrol makes a final extra contribution to the hybrid engine's manifold.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is car engines, where hybrid and manifold are parts; hybrid is the animal, and manifold is the adjective meaning many.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: manifold means many and various.

entries.clue: For starters, where are your social manners? (4)

indicatorNotes.For starters: the starters are the first letters

blocks.note: first letters of where, are, your, social

annotation.surface: A scolding at dinner about someone's lack of manners, starting with the first course.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For starters' sounds like the first course of a meal; it signals first letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plural synonym: a person's customary habits and behaviour, as in 'mend your ways'.

entries.clue: Currency leads to oblivion from lack of transparency (7)

blocks.note: a coma is a state of oblivion

annotation.surface: Money leads to ruin when the finances are kept hidden.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lack of transparency' reads as secretive finance; it is medical, a clouding of the eye.
annotation.definitionFit: A medical term: a leucoma is a white opaque patch on the cornea, where the eye loses its clearness.

entries.clue: Good girls may be shot (7)

annotation.definitionNote: a definition by example: shot is one kind of glass
annotation.surface: A dark hint that well-behaved girls could be gunned down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shot' suggests gunfire; it is the small drinking glass for spirits.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a shot glass is one kind of glass, so glasses may be shot.

entries.clue: Never mind inmates trotted out (2,6,6)

indicatorNotes.out: the letters come out in a new order

annotation.surface: Prisoners are paraded out, but it's nothing to worry about.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trotted out' reads as one phrasal verb; 'trotted' is fodder and 'out' alone is the indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Never mind' and 'it doesn't matter' both dismiss a concern.
